title: Billet / Michael Kutowski
excerpt: Billet is a free desktop board for the Markdown task files your coding agents write. For macOS, Windows, and Linux.
content_html:
One live board for the Markdown task files your coding agents write in your repos.

Download Get the skills

Completely free, no account needed. For macOS, Windows, and Linux. The skills are open source.

One task, start to finish

Task 16 in a sample project. Each step changes a few lines in its file, and the board follows within a second.

  1. You ask for a Markdown export. The agent checks the idea against the code and writes task 16. It lands in Proposed, since a decision about it is still open.

    "status"
    "proposed"

    "created"
    "2026-11-03"

    A new file, with the next ID from tasks.json.

  2. Once you make the decision, the task moves to Ready. Ask your agent to update it, or drag the card yourself.

    "status"
    "proposed""ready"

  3. The task is marked running on its branch, md-export. Its card glows and shows how long the agent has been at it.

    "status"
    "ready""in-progress"

    "started"
    null"2026-11-04"

    "running"
    null"2026-11-04T14:02:00+01:00"

    "branch"
    null"md-export"

  4. The agent checks the work and marks the task done. The running marker clears and the card moves to the top of Done.

    "status"
    "in-progress""done"

    "finished"
    null"2026-11-04"

    "running"
    "2026-11-04T14:02:00+01:00"null

    Plus one Unreleased entry in CHANGELOG.md.

Plain files in your repo

Each task is one Markdown file in docs/tasks/, with a small JSON header for status, order, and blockers. Your agents write them through the skills, and they stay in Git next to the code they describe.

Billet only watches those files. There is nothing to sync, no account, no server, and no database, and your files never leave your machine. A file it cannot read is listed by name with the reason, never hidden.

lantern/
└─ docs/tasks/
   ├─ tasks.json
   ├─ 0015-pin-notes-to-the-sidebar.md
   ├─ 0016-export-notes-as-a-markdown.md
   └─ 0017-import-an-exported-folder-back.md

Hand work to your agents

Selecting a task copies its ID and title, ready to paste into a session. Pick several and copy them as /billet-start commands, one per parallel session, or as one prompt.

Not sure what to do next? The die picks a random task that can start now.

Every project, one keystroke away

Add the folder that holds your projects, such as ~/Developer, and any project kept elsewhere. ⌘P, or the project’s name in the title strip, switches between them, recent ones first, and projects with nothing open are dimmed.

Keyboard-first: ⌘1 to ⌘5 switch views, T flips Home between Overview and Timeline, the arrow keys move through each view, and ? lists every shortcut.

Find, filter, and sort

Search every task’s text with ⌘F, in this project or across all of them, closed tasks included. Filter by area, tag, hardness, running, or can start, and sort by board order, ID, hardness, dates, or area. Each project keeps its own filter and sort.

The skills

Short instruction files your agent loads. Install the billet-* skills once, run billet-init in a project, then manage tasks by asking.

Finished tasks keep what was learned, so an agent can look up what earlier work found instead of finding it again.

billet-skillsOn GitHub, zlib license

Set up and plan

billet-init
Sets up a project once: creates the task folder and tells the project’s agents about it.

billet-add
Turns an idea into a task file, checked against the code and existing tasks.

billet-critique
Challenges a plan before work starts: weak spots, wrong assumptions, missing decisions.

billet-split
Breaks a large task into pieces only when they can really be worked on in parallel.

Work

billet-start
Starts or continues a task, asks open questions first, and marks it running on its branch.

billet-finish
Verifies the work, closes the task, and adds a changelog entry.

billet-merge
Merges a finished task’s branch, checks the result, closes the task, and removes its worktree.

billet-cancel
Drops a task with a reason and keeps its record.

Keep track

billet-list
Reports open tasks with their IDs, status, and hardness.

billet-leftovers
Checks whether recent work finished what it set out to do and files what is left.

billet-groom
Cleans up the board’s data and checks it is still accurate against the code.

billet-recall
Answers what earlier tasks and docs already know about a topic, with links.

Questions

Something missing? Find me on socials.

Do I need an AI agent to use it?

No. A task is a Markdown file with a small JSON header, so you can write one by hand. The skills just mean your agent keeps the files for you.

Which agents do the skills work with?

Any coding agent that supports skills. Run one like any other skill, for example /billet-add, or just ask your agent to add a task.

Can Billet change my tasks?

It never creates tasks, writes their text, or talks to a model. You can tidy by hand: drag a card to another status, mark its hardness, or clear a stale running marker. Those edits follow the skills’ rules, touch only the header, and never overwrite a newer change an agent just made.

How does it know an agent is working on a task?

When an agent starts a task, the start skill writes a running timestamp and the branch into the task’s header. Finishing clears it. Billet shows how long that has been and on which branch. If a session dies halfway, clear the stale marker from the task’s right-click menu.

Where are my tasks stored?

In each project’s docs/tasks/ folder, inside your repository. The folder is a setting, for projects that keep tasks somewhere else. Billet itself only keeps its own settings, such as recent projects, the current view, and the window position.

Can I use my own columns?

Yes. A tasks.json beside the task files lists the status columns in order. The defaults are proposed, ready, in-progress, done, and canceled.

Why is it free but not open source?

Billet is small on purpose: a Markdown viewer for the task files the skills write, with a board on top. The task format and skills are open source, so anyone can build a different view of the same files. The app itself shares its UI and platform layer with commercial projects of mine, so I keep that code private rather than publish it for one free app.

Why is it called Billet?

A billet is a written order that assigns someone a job, which is what a task file is. Pin them to a board and you get a billet board.

I’ve been using it for months now, and it works nicely for local task management. I wouldn’t go back to writing tasks by hand and working through them myself.

Download Billet

Completely free, with no account or paid tier. Your files stay on your machine and nothing is tracked. At startup Billet asks this site for the latest version number, which you can turn off in Settings.

  • macOS
  • Windows
  • Linux
Download Billet

The skills are available now. Get them on GitHub.

Check out my other projects

content_html_zh:
One live board for the Markdown task files your coding agents write in your repos.

Download Get the skills

Completely free, no account needed. For macOS, Windows, and Linux. The skills are open source.

One task, start to finish

Task 16 in a sample project. Each step changes a few lines in its file, and the board follows within a second.

  1. You ask for a Markdown export. The agent checks the idea against the code and writes task 16. It lands in Proposed, since a decision about it is still open. "status""proposed""created""2026-11-03" A new file, with the next ID from tasks.json.
  2. Once you make the decision, the task moves to Ready. Ask your agent to update it, or drag the card yourself. "status""proposed""ready"
  3. The task is marked running on its branch, md-export. Its card glows and shows how long the agent has been at it. "status""ready""in-progress""started"null"2026-11-04""running"null"2026-11-04T14:02:00+01:00""branch"null"md-export"
  4. The agent checks the work and marks the task done. The running marker clears and the card moves to the top of Done. "status""in-progress""done""finished"null"2026-11-04""running""2026-11-04T14:02:00+01:00"null Plus one Unreleased entry in CHANGELOG.md.

Plain files in your repo

Each task is one Markdown file in docs/tasks/, with a small JSON header for status, order, and blockers. Your agents write them through the skills, and they stay in Git next to the code they describe.

Billet only watches those files. There is nothing to sync, no account, no server, and no database, and your files never leave your machine. A file it cannot read is listed by name with the reason, never hidden.

lantern/
└─ docs/tasks/
   ├─ tasks.json
   ├─ 0015-pin-notes-to-the-sidebar.md
   ├─ 0016-export-notes-as-a-markdown.md
   └─ 0017-import-an-exported-folder-back.md

Hand work to your agents

Selecting a task copies its ID and title, ready to paste into a session. Pick several and copy them as /billet-start commands, one per parallel session, or as one prompt.

Not sure what to do next? The die picks a random task that can start now.

Every project, one keystroke away

Add the folder that holds your projects, such as ~/Developer, and any project kept elsewhere. ⌘P, or the project’s name in the title strip, switches between them, recent ones first, and projects with nothing open are dimmed.

Keyboard-first: ⌘1 to ⌘5 switch views, T flips Home between Overview and Timeline, the arrow keys move through each view, and ? lists every shortcut.

Find, filter, and sort

Search every task’s text with ⌘F, in this project or across all of them, closed tasks included. Filter by area, tag, hardness, running, or can start, and sort by board order, ID, hardness, dates, or area. Each project keeps its own filter and sort.

技能

Finished tasks keep what was learned, so an agent can look up what earlier work found instead of finding it again.

billet-skillsOn GitHub, zlib license

Set up and plan

billet-initSets up a project once: creates the task folder and tells the project’s agents about it.

billet-addTurns an idea into a task file, checked against the code and existing tasks.

billet-critiqueChallenges a plan before work starts: weak spots, wrong assumptions, missing decisions.

billet-splitBreaks a large task into pieces only when they can really be worked on in parallel.

Work

billet-startStarts or continues a task, asks open questions first, and marks it running on its branch.

billet-finishVerifies the work, closes the task, and adds a changelog entry.

billet-mergeMerges a finished task’s branch, checks the result, closes the task, and removes its worktree.

billet-cancelDrops a task with a reason and keeps its record.

Keep track

billet-listReports open tasks with their IDs, status, and hardness.

billet-leftoversChecks whether recent work finished what it set out to do and files what is left.

billet-groomCleans up the board’s data and checks it is still accurate against the code.

billet-recallAnswers what earlier tasks and docs already know about a topic, with links.

问题

缺少什么吗？ Find me on socials.

Do I need an AI agent to use it?

No. A task is a Markdown file with a small JSON header, so you can write one by hand. The skills just mean your agent keeps the files for you.

Which agents do the skills work with?

Any coding agent that supports skills. Run one like any other skill, for example /billet-add, or just ask your agent to add a task.

Can Billet change my tasks?

It never creates tasks, writes their text, or talks to a model. You can tidy by hand: drag a card to another status, mark its hardness, or clear a stale running marker. Those edits follow the skills’ rules, touch only the header, and never overwrite a newer change an agent just made.

How does it know an agent is working on a task?

When an agent starts a task, the start skill writes a running timestamp and the branch into the task’s header. Finishing clears it. Billet shows how long that has been and on which branch. If a session dies halfway, clear the stale marker from the task’s right-click menu.

Where are my tasks stored?

In each project’s docs/tasks/ folder, inside your repository. The folder is a setting, for projects that keep tasks somewhere else. Billet itself only keeps its own settings, such as recent projects, the current view, and the window position.

Can I use my own columns?

是的。 A tasks.json beside the task files lists the status columns in order. The defaults are proposed, ready, in-progress, done, and canceled.

Why is it free but not open source?

Billet is small on purpose: a Markdown viewer for the task files the skills write, with a board on top. The task format and skills are open source, so anyone can build a different view of the same files. The app itself shares its UI and platform layer with commercial projects of mine, so I keep that code private rather than publish it for one free app.

Why is it called Billet?

A billet is a written order that assigns someone a job, which is what a task file is. Pin them to a board and you get a billet board.

I’ve been using it for months now, and it works nicely for local task management. I wouldn’t go back to writing tasks by hand and working through them myself.

Download Billet

Completely free, with no account or paid tier. Your files stay on your machine and nothing is tracked. At startup Billet asks this site for the latest version number, which you can turn off in Settings.
